notes:
Summary and key notes:
- Primary pain: production incidents during seasonal peaks (holiday spikes + product launches) where queues balloon and agent assist/rerank tasks time out. Reported symptoms: long wait times, API timeouts for tool-calls, agent context lost when requests retry.
- Targets: 95th pct latency <250ms for agent-assist lookups; <800ms for tool-calls (external system invocation) during steady state. During peak bursts (observed up to 3k concurrent agents; synthetic replay shows instantaneous bursts up to 6k requests/s) need graceful degradation rather than hard failures.
- Throughput: baseline 400 req/s for summarization/rerank pipelines; peak replay target 2-6k rps for short windows (2-15 minutes).
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for Dedicated reserved capacity for peak SLAs but wants tooling to optimize unit cost (batching, quantization, cache).
- Model preferences: open to MPT-style and Llama2 variants but must be able to fallback to smaller quantized models for bursts; interested in Redwood's catalog and Verified perf profiles.
- Routing/fallback needs: automated fallback to cached responses or quantized tiny model; region-aware routing to avoid cross-border residency issues; ability to pin different model versions for canary rollouts.
- Observability/ops: token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency heatmaps, tracing to tie timeouts to specific tool-calls. Must have audit logs for every request (CISO ask).
- POC configuration: run 48h stress test on Dedicated pool (n1-standard equivalent + A100 forecast), replay historical peak traces, enable prefix caching, test KV cache warmup time. Need Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching windows and kernel selection.
- Security: strict SSO/SAML SSO, SOC2 required, on-prem option desirable for EU data residency. KMS/HSM for key management.
- Quote from Director of Ops: "We can survive small outages but the holiday spikes cost us revenue and SLA credits — we need predictable behavior when queues back up."
- Linked artifacts: pricing deck, sec FAQ, POC dataset manifest.
- Risk areas: legal wants explicit data residency controls; infra wants deterministic cold-start behavior for KV cache.
- Success criteria for close: pass security checklist, demonstrate <1% error rate during 48h stress run with defined fallbacks, signed reserved capacity contract.
